title: kernel-probing-concurrency-smoothing-and-decode-handoff-plan
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Since integrating FlashAttention v3 we observed intermittent latency spikes and occasional decode jitter when the runtime switches kernels for long-context requests. Root causes appear to be a mix of kernel warmup cost, workspace allocation jitter, and contention on the kernel prober thread when multiple concurrent prefill requests race to prime v3 code paths. Goal: implement a low-risk smoothing layer and probing schedule that reduces oscillation during bursts, preserves v2 fallback safety, and provides actionable telemetry for future autotuning. Deliverables: (1) probing concurrency limiter and staggered probe windows; (2) decode-handoff handshake with a short warm-cache grace period; (3) metrics and dashboards to detect oscillation events; (4) a canary rollout playbook and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for 2k-token generations does not increase by more than 5% in standard perf harness compared to current baseline
Oscillation events (kernel thrash: >3 kernel switches per request) reduced by >= 80% in burst simulation
Canary rollout demonstrates stable behavior on 5% of traffic for 48 hours with automated rollback on error rate increase > 1%
New telemetry hooks emit probe start/stop, probe duration, warm-cache-hits, and handoff-latency; dashboard panels populated
work_plan: Week 1: Implement probing concurrency limiter (token bucket) and staggered probe windows; unit tests and microbench harnesses
Week 2: Add decode-handoff handshake: short grace window (~50ms) where KV cache prefill is preferred and kernel switch is delayed unless required; integrate with priority queue
Week 3: Add telemetry spans and counters; create dashboard panels and alert thresholds; run synthetic burst tests across instance types
Week 4: Canary rollout to 'canary-5pct' with runtime-1.22; monitor and iterate; prepare rollback automation and runbook
implementation_notes: Design trade-offs: conservative approach favors user-visible latency over potential unit-cost savings from aggressive v3 activation; will expose flag to tune aggressiveness
Concurrency limiter implemented in runtime/kernel_prober.cc as an async guard with per-GPU and global modes
Handshake uses a new decode_handoff token exchanged via the request context to avoid global locks
Fallback behavior: immediate fallback to v2 if workspace allocation fails or if probe duration exceeds a safety timeout (default 200ms)
Benchmarks: use perf/harnesses/long_context and perf/harnesses/prefill_burst suites; compare v2-only, v3-only, and hybrid with smoothing enabled
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: added latency for cold-start probes could slightly increase tail latency. Mitigation: default to low concurrency (1-2 probes) and keep grace window short; expose runtime flag for emergency off
Risk: misattribution in telemetry when handoff overlaps with retry. Mitigation: include unique probe IDs and correlation IDs in spans
Risk: rollback automation may not trigger if monitoring thresholds are mis-configured. Mitigation: run failure injection during canary to validate alerts and rollback paths
testing_plan: Unit tests for concurrency limiter and token behavior
Integration tests simulating 50-300 concurrent prefill requests with variable seq lengths
Chaos test: inject OOM/alloc failures and assert correct v2 fallback
Long-run canary for 72h (min 48h before considering rollout) with synthetic and real traffic mixes
